intro: Kefalonia's great tree stands on the Omala plateau, inland from Argostoli, a short walk from the monastery of the island's patron saint. Tradition says Saint Gerasimos planted the plane himself and dug the well at its root. Its rings tell a measured story instead. A study presented in 2023 put it at about 448 years, counted from the outer wood because the trunk is hollow, and that study led to its declaration as a Preserved Natural Monument in 2024.
meta_description: Kefalonia's Plane of Saint Gerasimos on the Omala plateau: about 450 years old by ring count, hollow, by tradition planted by the island's patron saint.
question_meta: Kefalonia's oldest known tree is the Plane of Saint Gerasimos at Omala, put at about 448 years in 2022 by a ring study of its hollow trunk.
question_answer: The oldest known tree on Kefalonia is the oriental plane of Saint Gerasimos on the Omala plateau, estimated at about 448 years in 2022, roughly 450 today. The figure comes from a ring count of the outer wood, because the trunk is hollow.
question_context: The age comes from a dendrochronology study presented at the Panhellenic Forestry Conference in October 2023, at Loutra Aidipsou by a team of seven researchers, and Greek authorities used it the following year to declare the tree a Preserved Natural Monument. The island's tradition says something different in kind rather than in number. It holds that Saint Gerasimos, Kefalonia's patron saint, planted the plane and dug the well at its root. The ring count is an estimate, since the hollow centre is gone, and the tradition is a tradition, so neither is offered here as proof of the other. The tree is 5.37 metres round and 24 metres tall, recorded by the Greek Tree Registry in September 2024. It stands in an open square about 500 metres from the monastery gate, free to visit, and you need a car to reach the plateau. If you know the tradition as the monastery tells it, or anything the study left out, tell us.

faq.q: Did Saint Gerasimos really plant the plane at Omala?
faq.a: That is the island's tradition, and the ring count neither proves nor disproves it. What has been measured is the tree's age, about 448 years in 2022, counted from its outer wood.

faq.q: How do you get to the Plane of Saint Gerasimos?
faq.a: By car, inland from Argostoli to the Omala plateau. The tree stands in an open square about 500 metres from the entrance of the Monastery of Agios Gerasimos, with no ticket or gate.

location.address: Omala plateau near Valsamata, about 500 m from the entrance of the Monastery of Agios Gerasimos, Kefalonia

trees.story:
Researchers counted this plane's rings and arrived at about 448 years in 2022. They had to work from the outer wood, because the centre of the trunk is hollow, so the figure is an estimate rather than a birth certificate. It puts the tree at roughly 450 today.

Kefalonia tells it differently. By the island's tradition, the plane was planted by Saint Gerasimos, the island's patron saint, whose monastery stands about 500 metres away on the Omala plateau, and the well at its root is said to be his work too. The ring count is science and the planting is tradition. This page gives you both and does not pretend one proves the other.

The study was presented at the Panhellenic Forestry Conference in October 2023, and it did more than settle a question. It was the basis on which Greek authorities declared the tree a Preserved Natural Monument in August 2024.

The Greek Tree Registry recorded it a month later at 5.37 metres round and 24 metres tall. Those are good numbers for a plane, not record ones. What sets this tree apart is that somebody actually measured its age, which few old trees with a saint's name attached can say.

It stands in an open square on the plateau, inland from Argostoli, with no ticket and no gate. You will need a car. The monastery and the tree are a short walk apart, so see them together.

official_register.name: Greek Tree Registry, Friends of Hellenic National Parks (entry 81); declared Preserved Natural Monument by decision 379069/13-08-2024 (Government Gazette B 4903)

trees.access: Free. Registry lists the land as a square (open, accessible) on the Omala plateau, about 500 m from the monastery gate; no ticket or permission recorded.

trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its hollow trunk, 5.37 metres round, with a well at its root. It stands in an open square on the Omala plateau, about 500 metres from the entrance of the Monastery of Agios Gerasimos.
